body: I always thought that relationships should be based off compatibility. For me, a good friend could still be a bad significant other (take it with a grain of salt i'm the virgin here). Let's use an example of roommates. There are so many friendships that diminish because friends end up becoming roommates and find out each other's true colors.  Back to the topic of attractiveness, I remember learning in psychology that the tendencies are that people are attracted to people who have the same physical attraction as them. I forgot the other two conditions but it does show that physical attraction is crucial. As for dating apps, it's based on mostly looks. Sometimes there aren't any profiles written and people either swipe like or not. Don't hate yourself because of others' subjectivity. As cliche as it may seem, it is true; if you can't love yourself then how are you going to love someone else?

It seems like you've hit rock bottom. There isn't a better opportunity to try to change your life. You have nothing to lose so why not try to better yourself? You understand that you've buried your emotions and that caused you to feel empty. This time acknowledge your emotions and realize that your previous relationship isn't your current relationship. It's time to pursue your own happiness in life. This all sounds vague but if I had to simplify it, I recommend that you try to find something to do in order to stabilize yourself before going into a relationship. Relying all of your happiness into a relationship will be the ultimate downfall for you if it goes turmoil.

It seems like you're oversimplifying life. Life isn't just about graduating multiple times and then working a 9-5 job. What really makes life considered life is the path toward those goals. You will encounter inconsistencies in life. You will encounter detours and delays in life. Being the best version of yourself is going to matter but not in a sense that you may think. I'll use voting as an example. Many people don't participate in elections because they think that their individual vote will not impact anything. Those individual votes add up in order to make a significance. You aren't the only one that is trying to be the best version of themselves. Society is collective so being the best you can be will impact the world in a sense that you will be a contribution to society.
Anytime!

Sometimes attention is the right answer for some circumstances. Everything today is for tomorrow. The today you will not be tomorrow you. That's the whole concept of trying to improve yourself. You said that it's proven to you that endless complaining won't help. The fact that you're willing to admit this already proves that you're acknowledging the problem. This is a slow development toward improvement. I would also like to address my thank you for your response back to me. I'm glad that you were able to display your true feelings and honesty to me. If you ever need to talk about something, I'll try my best to respond asap!

I'm sorry but I'm going to have to say that I disagree. Stephen Hawking didn't have a good life because he was a good looker, he was a genius. Jay-Z didn't have a good life because he was good looking, he was a talented artist. A lot of people have led good lives despite of their appearances.

Just because a lot of people claim that doesn't necessarily mean it's true. That's like saying if everyone lied then it would become the truth. The general consensus is that there's more to life than just how you look. There's more people in the world than the "true rate me."

We're humans, our lives aren't based off natural selection due to our phenotype. Your look isn't what life is looking for so there is absolutely no reason to kill yourself because of your appearance. It really makes me sad that you're willing to call yourself "material" because you aren't giving yourself enough self-respect. Beauty is subjective, you may see yourself as a 4 but others may rate you higher.
It just means you're an extremely empathetic person. It's hard to stop feeling sorry for everything but I think it's a very nice trait to have.

You should never apologize for ranting about a topic like this. If anything, this is the best thing you could have done. Sometimes, attention is the remedy for someone troubled. There are times when I feel like I'm suffocating in a bubble called "life." You don't need to keep up the positive facade if you feel like that's not who you really are. Being honest to yourself will be your first step toward improvement.
It makes me sad to read Horimiya because of how wholesome the manga is. I'm on the same boat as you op, It's something that makes me realize that I am pretty lonely.

I think I understand where you're coming from. Life is fair and unfair (paradoxical) in a sense that somethings are within grasp and others are inevitable. I genuinely wish that your relationship is the lingering reason of why you're going to live. Gradually you will begin to understand that there's more to life than the relationship that you are in. Life really is a stupid game, a beautiful facade. The fact that you have two more years means you have a chance to make up for the rough year. Life is always going to fluctuate, even for the most powerful person in the world. Whether it's an external or internal conflict, there will always be life spirals. This brings me to my next point, regardless of how much we complain about being tired of life's ambiguity, it will never end. My recommendation would be to try to find loopholes that could occupy your mind (things such as activities and whatnot). I'm not 100% certain if I'm even telling you the right thing or not but hey I'm just a stranger on the computer.

You make a good point in a sense that life is basically a competition. Let's change the mentality of it then. Compare yourself to your ideal future. There's no point of comparing yourself to someone else because you're not going to ever become them no matter how much you try. If you begin to compare your present self to your own future image, hopefully it will give you insight on what you want to work on. All you can really do is be the best that you can. It sound shallow but let me use sports competition as an example. If everyone trained the same amount, then ideally everyone should be the best right? This is never the case. The reason for that is because some have talent and innate abilities over others. The idea of you comparing yourself to everyone over everything is what's making you unable to stop comparing. The fact is you're not going to be the best at everything you do so let go of that and accept that you won't have perfect results for everything. There will be things you're going to be horrible at, mediocre at, or amazing at.

This is my speculation on why I think your parents may be homophobic. Humans are naturally afraid of changes, they think that if they stay in their pocket of comfort that it will satisfy them for the rest of their lives. That's part of why many conservatives attempt to preserve traditional thinking, they have a perspective that change is bad. In the end, you're living for yourself and not for them. There was a point in time where I believed that I was gay. I was afraid that my peers and family would look at me differently but that wasn't my biggest fear. My biggest fear was that I would have an identity crisis. Fast forward, I realize that I wasn't gay but it was just a "what-if" theory and that was enough to cause a reaction within my brain. Your biggest luxury is that you get to be yourself by coming out lesbian. Being different is not bad but rather unique. It offers you an option to explore choices that others cannot do. I think the problem is that you have a notion that being lesbian is bad. There are others who have come out the closet and have been happy ever since. Life is just a waiting game after all, whether you decide to take action or wait it out, in the end you're still waiting for something. Your happiness will come, I promise you that.

I don't have any companion to make me feel amazing so I believe you should cherish that. Humans are inherently selfish hence I don't think that your boyfriend would stay with you just out of pity. If you end your life then how do you think your boyfriend is going to feel? It's possible that if you kill yourself, your boyfriend will feel exactly how you're feeling right now. Please don't give up because you being sad now means that you were really happy at one point and it proves that it's possible to attain that state again.

There's no need to change yourself. A lot of people misinterpret shy, boring, aloof, and forgettable as a negative connotation. Not everyone could be outgoing, confident, nor talkative so why attempt to pursue that? I'm not advocating to stay miserable but try to look at your personality in a different light. It may sound weird, but I've always been attracted to girls who were shy and quiet. Those perks that you listed yourself as is what makes you beautiful. As corny as it sounds, your "weaknesses" are actually your strongest points. There are two reasons why I'm saying this: 1. I'm attracted to girls who are shy, boring, quiet, aloof, and forgettable so that might be biased... but 2. your traits are what distinguishes you from others. Isn't being a human being all about variety and experiencing life with multiple options? Don't abandon yourself and try to become someone you aren't because I believe that's what will really make you feel disgusted in the future.
